name: Kids myopia control
summary: How expat families manage childhood myopia in Singapore — ortho-K, atropine, myopia-control lenses, review cadence, and school-year timing around prescription changes.
body:
Singapore’s high myopia rates push many parents beyond single-vision glasses. Optometrists and ophthalmologists offer atropine drops, orthokeratology overnight lenses, and specialised myopia-control spectacles or soft lenses. Choice depends on age, prescription progression, and overnight-lens readiness.

## Decision points
- Progressive myopia vs stable mild prescription
- Atropine concentration and side-effect monitoring
- Ortho-K hygiene discipline for overnight wear
- Daytime myopia-control glasses vs contacts
- Review interval during growth spurts / exam seasons

Outdoor time still matters — clinics often pair optical plans with lifestyle advice.

## How to choose
Prefer clinicians who show axial-length or progression charts, not only a new glasses quote. Ask who handles after-hours ortho-K irritation. Confirm international-school calendar buffers before changing modalities mid-term.

## Practical tip
Photograph the current prescription and next review date in your phone wallet. Lost glasses week before exams is a common scramble.
